craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra of equation; vyabhicāri exultation at five-said-once. Sanskrit-first: duṣkara (HARD-TO-DO — kept hard); pañca-pada-ekārtha (FIVE terms ONE referent — kept five, per C1). Rows: 9 (hardest/highest/freedom/lordship/awareness drummed — five-said-once), 1 (‘awareness-nature’ closes — jñāna-rūpa last of five), 3 (hardest=highest=freest: equation interlock). Close: ‘awareness-nature’. Rupture: semicolon (deed turns to equation). Rejected: ‘duty’ — killed: hardness is the doctrine; ‘liberation’ alone — killed: five kept five; ‘consciousness itself’ — killed: awareness-nature kept technical. Read aloud: WHAT is HARD-est TO-do IS-his — AND-none IS-high-ER … THAT it-SELF is FREE-dom, LORD-ship, a-WARE-ness-NA-ture.

lines: What is hardest to do is His — and none is higher;
that itself is freedom, lordship, awareness-nature.
l4.sanskrit_cite: atidurghaṭakāritvam asyānuttaram eva yat | etad eva svatantratvam aisvaryaṃ bodharūpatā

reads_against.argmap: What five names share one referent? → Five terms, one referent: hard = unsurpassed = autonomy = lordship = awareness-form.
c1_essence: Hardest deed, unsurpassed: autonomy, lordship, awareness-form in one.
